product_from_film: Librar is a school-library management system that identifies books from shelf photos and provides collection and usage insights.
explains_well: The shelf-photo phone view leads into a catalog and chart, giving the AI-librarian claim a concrete setup task.
unclear: The film does not show how an identified book reaches a student or how the catalog work leads to the claimed increase in reading.
scenario: A presenter explains staffing needs, demonstrates shelf-photo setup through UI inserts and claims time savings and higher reading rates.
product_clear_basis: At 21–23s a phone captures shelves and shows a result state, followed by catalog organization at 25s; the broad library-system label appears at 13–16s.

sound.detail: The draft broadly explains staffing, shelf-photo setup, organization, insights, time savings and reading goals. Product names and several phrases are misrecognized; captions and UI support the main reading. No validated listening, delivery, music, effects or sync assessment.
sound.visual_relation: V01–V06; visual captions support the explanatory script.

categories.finding: Staffing problem → AI library system → shelf-photo catalog setup → staff benefit → reading mission → book handoff and URL.
A seated presenter in front of books immediately establishes the library setting; captions begin the problem statement.
School-library staff and students are explicit. Shelf-photo identification gives the product a concrete function by 22–25s.
Statistic circles fill, text changes scale and UI overlays replace one another over the presenter. Page turns and the final handoff provide physical action. Exact transition paths are unverified.
Shelf imagery bridges the staffing statistic and photo setup; the final book handoff returns software benefits to a physical reading object.
Dark red-brown shelves, pale gray clothing and orange branding create a warm library identity.
Captions carry the explanation and benefit words are large. Phone result text and catalog details are small compared with the presenter.
The draft supports the broad pitch with wording errors resolved only where captions are visible. Voice delivery remains unchecked.
Music character and structure are unverified.
Effects and their sources are unverified.

categories.finding: Captions and UI preserve the main proposition silently. The link from organization to actual student use remains implied.
The presenter anchors the frame, but UI overlays are brief and small. The book handoff has a clear physical focus.
The setup task gets about eight seconds, while staffing and impact claims occupy most of the film. One named book could make the brief demo easier to follow.
The staffing problem is answered by collection automation and time claims. The student-reading goal ends in a handoff image rather than a measured usage story.
Concern about unmet reading needs shifts toward helpful automation and a tangible book handoff; audience response is unmeasured.
Bookshelves, photos, catalog and physical books connect the sequence, but no specific title is traced through the workflow.
The staffing statistic, hundreds-of-hours saving, doubled reading rates and literacy goal are claims. Identification accuracy, study basis and actual student outcomes were not checked.
Shelf-photo catalog setup and the orange pixel-like Librar mark distinguish the offer.
Trace one title from shelf to student.
categories.experiment: Show a shelf photo identifying one book, its catalog record and a student finding or borrowing that title.

categories.finding: For Tin, show one asset across intake, organization and use.

lessons.keep: Connect a physical source, such as shelves, to the resulting organized digital view.
